Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 LAAS.No.7 of 2024
Judgment:
(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard Sri Ch.Ravinder, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant No.3.

Though respondent Nos.2 and 3, who are claimant Nos.1 and 2,
respectively, are served with notices, they did not choose to enter appearance through an Advocate.
Perused the entire material available on record.

2. This appeal is filed under Section 74 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for brevity, 'the Act'), challenging the order dated 08.12.2023 passed by the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority for the State of Telangana at Hyderabad (for brevity, hereinafter referred to as "the Authority under the Act') in LAOP.No.72 of 2018.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority for the State of Telangana
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. The undisputed facts of the case, shorn off unnecessary details, are that land to an extent of Acs.2.08 guntas in Sy.No.182 of Samudralingapur Village, Gambhirraopet Mandal, Rajanna- 2 AKS, J & LNA, J Sircilla District, was acquired for excavation of Gravity Canal from Malakpet Reservoir to Singasamudram; that preliminary notification under Section 11(1) of the Act was published in Telangana State Gazette on 01.08.2015; that after conducting the award enquiry, the Land Acquisition Officer passed Award, vide proceedings No.H/121/2017, dated 02.02.2018, fixing the market value of the acquired land @ Rs.5,22,530/- per acre.
The name of the claimant for the acquired land was shown as Eddandi Linga Reddy in the Award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

However, as the appellant herein raised a dispute claiming 50% share in the compensation,
the Land Acquisition Officer has referred the matter to the competent Authority under the Act under Section 64 read with Section 76 of the Act.
The same was accordingly numbered as LAOP.No.72 of 2018 on the file of the Authority under the Act.

4. Before the Authority under the Act, on behalf of respondent Nos.2 and 3/claimant Nos.1 and 2,
P.Ws.1 and 2 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-9 were marked.
On behalf of appellant/claimant No.3, no oral or documentary evidence was adduced.

sentences.text: The Authority under the Act disposed of the said LAOP, answering the Reference in favour of claimant No.1 in respect of Ac.1.00 guntas of land in Sy.No.182 and closed the Reference in respect of Ac.0.04 guntas of land in Sy.No.182.

The Authority under the Act held that claimant No.1 is entitled to compensation of Rs.5,22,530/- for Ac.1.00 guntas of land in Sy.No.182 of Samudralingapur Village, along with interest accrued thereon.
The compensation amount of Rs.52,253/- in respect of Ac.0.04 guntas of land was directed to be deposited till a claim is made for the same.

Challenging the said order passed by the Authority under the Act, the present Appeal is filed by claimant No.3.
6.

It is the case of the appellant/claimant No.3 in her Claim Petition that originally, her grandfather-Mallaiah was the absolute owner of several agricultural properties including the acquired lands admeasuring Acs.2.08 guntas in Sy.No.182/B; that after his death, his legal heirs partitioned the said properties, in which claimant No.1 got several agricultural lands including the acquired land to an extent of Ac.1.04 guntas; that claimant No.1 got married to the mother of claimant No.3; that claimant No.3 is natural born 4 AKS, J & LNA, J daughter of claimant No.1 through his legally wedded wife; that after the birth of claimant No.3, claimant No.1 gave divorce to his wife, i.e., mother of claimant No.3; that as alimony, claimant No.1 transferred some agricultural lands including the subject acquired land to an extent of Ac.1.04 guntas in Sy.No.182 in favour of the mother of claimant No.3; and that later, claimant No.1 kept one Pushpalatha as concubine.

It is further averred that under the guise of executing mortgage deed with the bank, claimant No.1 fraudulently obtained the signatures of the mother of claimant No.3 before the Sub-Registrar and transferred the properties including the acquired land to an extent of Ac.1.04 guntas in his name and in the name of his second wife under two registered sale deeds.
7. Further, it is the case of the appellant/claimant No.3 that she was a minor at the time of execution of the aforesaid documents and as such, the same does not bind her.
Therefore, she is entitled to 50% share in the compensation amount granted in respect of said extent of Ac.1.04 guntas of land.

8. On the other hand, claimant No.1 filed Claim Petition inter alia stating that at the time of giving divorce to mother of claimant 5 AKS, J & LNA, J No.3, as alimony, he gave her some properties including the acquired land to an extent of Ac.1.04 guntas and later, got married another woman by name Pushpalatha.

Thereafter, the mother of claimant No.3 due to her necessities, sold the said extent of Ac.1.04 guntas of land to his second wife and as such, claimant No.3, who was a minor at that time, is not entitled to claim any title over the said property as she failed to make claim within three years of her attaining majority.

Hence, claimant No.1 prayed to award compensation to him dismissing the claim of claimant No.3.
9.
Apropos the rival contentions of both the parties, it is to be seen that the relationship between claimant No.1 and claimant No.3 being father and daughter is undisputed.

The material available on record goes to show that claimant No.3 filed suit in O..S.No.25 of 2003 against claimant No.1 claiming share in land admeasuring Ac.1.04 guntas in Sy.No.182 (subject acquired land) and the same was dismissed.

Subsequently, claimant No.3 filed another suit- O.S.No.22 of 2015 and the said Yeddandi Pakala Rajitha vs Special Deputy Collector on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138826928/
2 suit was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to her to file a comprehensive suit, vide orders dated 29.11.2016.

sentences.text: Accordingly, claimant No.3 filed suit-O.S.No.1 of 6 AKS, J & LNA, J 2017 against claimant No.1 on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Sircilla, seeking the reliefs of partition and separate possession and for declaring the sale deeds said to have been executed by her mother in favour of claimant No.1 and his second wife as not binding on her and her mother, is pending consideration.

10. It is relevant to note that in the suit-O.S.No.1 of 2017, the civil Court by docket order, dated 27.01.2017, granted ad-interim injunction restraining the defendants therein, i.e., claimant No.1, his second wife and four others from alienating the suit schedule properties till disposal of the suit.
The said order is said to be subsisting as of now.

11. The Authority under the Act rejected the claim filed by appellant on the ground that she failed to enter into witness box to deny the documentary evidence produced by claimant No.1 (P.W-1),
though she filed claim petition in the year 2018 and further, she failed to produce any documents in support of her claim.
12.

Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the claim of the appellant was rejected only on the ground that she failed to 7 AKS, J & LNA, J produce any documentary evidence in support of her claim.

He further submitted that an opportunity may be given to the appellant to produce the evidence in support of her claim, as admittedly, the suit filed by her with regard to the subject land before the competent civil court is pending adjudication.

13. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and also in view of the fact that the Authority under the Act has rejected the claim of the appellant observing that she failed to enter into witness box and also did not produce any documentary evidence in support of her claim and now that the appellant is seeking an opportunity to produce the relevant documentary evidence before the Authority under the Act, this Court, without going into the merits of the case, deems it appropriate to remand the matter to the Authority under the Act for fresh adjudication duly taking into consideration the pendency of the suit-O.S.No.1 of 2017 filed by the appellant.

14. Accordingly, this Appeal is allowed, setting aside the impugned order and the matter is remanded to the Authority under the Act for fresh adjudication of the L.A.O.P., after giving an 8 AKS, J & LNA, J opportunity of hearing to both the parties and to adduce oral and documentary evidence, if any, in support of their respective claims and to pass appropriate orders afresh in accordance with law.
15.
As a sequel, Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
No costs.
_ _ _ A B H I N A N D K U M A R S H A V I L I , J
LAXMI NARAYANA ALISHETTY, J Dated:08.11.2024
